hook.line: Just 14 years after its release, two researchers independently proved that the first player wins by starting in the middle.
hook.say: Let’s drop into the history of Connect Four!

ch.say: It came from an American toy company.
p: In 1974 the American company Milton Bradley released “Connect Four”.
A vertical four-in-a-row where gravity drops the pieces, it became a hit with children and adults everywhere.

tl: Allen and Allis each prove a first-player win
Spreads to electronic games and TV

ch.t: Four in a row, with gravity
ch.say: Pieces always drop to the bottom.
ch.cap: 7 columns × 6 rows: four in a row in any direction wins
p: All you choose is the column — beautifully simple.
But pieces stack from the bottom, so you must plan the squares you want your rival to fill.

cards: You may also pop your own piece out of the bottom row
Larger boards such as 8×7 are studied too
The grand old line-up game — no gravity

ch.say: A small board with a huge number of positions!
cards: A Dutch researcher who analysed Connect Four and gomoku
An American researcher who found the winning strategy almost at the same time

ch.say: Tap a card to flip it!
cards: Does the first player always win?
With perfect play, yes — but only by starting in the centre column
